title: A low-dimensional dynamical basis for tongue shape control
abstract: arXiv:2610.23456v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Speech production involves the control of a high-dimensional articulatory system with many degrees-of-freedom, but a widespread hypothesis is that speakers navigate this complexity using a set of lower-dimensional control variables. Common candidates for these control variables include individual articulators (e.g. tongue body) and abstract tract variables (e.g. tongue body constriction location), but identifying the most appropriate coordinate system for articulatory control remains an open question. In this study, we advance a model in which holistic tongue shape modes represent a potential low-dimensional control basis for a simple dynamical law. We first discover empirical tongue shape modes in a cross-speaker coordinate space and then fit the model to ultrasound data on monophthongal vowels from 36 speakers of British English. translated_title: 舌形控制的低维动力学基础
translated_abstract: 言语产生涉及对具有众多自由度的高维发音系统的控制，但一个被广泛接受的假设是，说话者通过一组较低维度的控制变量来驾驭这种复杂性。这些控制变量的常见候选包括单个发音器官（如舌体）和抽象的声道变量（如舌体收窄位置），但确定发音控制最合适的坐标系仍然是一个悬而未决的问题。在本研究中，我们提出了一种模型，其中整体性舌形模式代表一个简单动力学定律的潜在低维控制基础。我们首先在跨说话者的坐标空间中发现经验性的舌形模式，然后将该模型拟合到来自36名英国英语说话者的单元音超声波数据上。拟合到这些随时间变化模式的三维线性点吸引子恢复了舌……
tldr: 该研究提出以整体舌形模式作为低维控制基础，并通过三维线性点吸引子的简单动力学模型成功拟合36名说话者的舌部超声波数据，为言语产生的低维发音控制提供了新证据。
en_tdlr: This study proposes holistic tongue shape modes as a low-dimensional control basis, showing that a simple three-dimensional linear point-attractor dynamical law fitted to ultrasound data from 36 speakers captures tongue shape control in speech production.
